summary: Olivia Chow's Instagram record on social services centers on expanded public services, support for vulnerable populations, and stronger funding for non-profits and front-line workers. Chow pledges to keep all 100 Toronto Public Library branches open seven days a week, create 24/7 respite spaces and wrap-around services for unhoused people, increase core funding for non-profits, and protect unionized public-service jobs (Cszj-OQtdG9, CsHejOWP0rO, Cs7XZJHAug5, CrtSNhOgByS). Chow supports the Toronto Community Crisis Service and its city-wide expansion, culturally appropriate health services, and supports for survivors of intimate partner and gender-based violence (CuX95hrA4Qv, CswRXNBAo-m, Cujn8P6utFZ, Cr33PZjPo8E). Earlier records emphasize child care expansion, school nutrition, youth employment, and senior care (tlEZvnutGS, tTEEA0OtEL, ugKSbCutDk, uJqN2uOtLA). Chow also voices support for 2SLGBTQI+ communities and opposition to Islamophobia, antisemitism, and homophobia (Cs9ZwzVPU-L, Cuh98p0PPkX, CtSF49tP4K6).

key_positions.stance: Supports expanding Toronto Public Library hours so all 100 branches open seven days a week
Supports treating homelessness as an emergency and creating 24/7 respite spaces with wrap-around supports
Supports expanding the Toronto Community Crisis Service city-wide so appropriate supports are available during crises
Supports increasing core funding for non-profits and protecting unionized public-service jobs
Supports addressing intimate partner and gender-based violence through services and reconciliation-focused supports
Supports 2SLGBTQI+ communities and opposes Islamophobia, antisemitism, and homophobia/transphobia
Supports expanded child care, school nutrition programs, after-school care, and youth employment programs
Supports caring for seniors via accessible transit, community housing, and affordable property taxes
Supports culturally sensitive health services and prioritizing the healthcare system

key_actions.action: Announced a plan to expand Toronto Public Library hours to seven days a week at all 100 branches
Met with Toronto Community Crisis Service partner organizations at TAIBU Community Health Centre to discuss city-wide expansion
Met with YWCA Toronto to discuss supportive housing and intimate partner violence
Joined the launch of the 'Toronto For All' anti-Islamophobia campaign
Held a press conference on the Vital Signs report concerning child poverty in Toronto
Announced a school food program expansion alongside Frances Lankin
Joined picket line in solidarity with CUPE 233 workers at Toronto Metropolitan University
Raised awareness for 360kids, a group serving young people in crisis
